skill.name: macos-spm-app-packaging
skill.description: Create SwiftPM-based macOS app scaffolds, build .app bundles, run local launch loops, and prepare signing, notarization, and Sparkle appcast workflows without an Xcode project.
skill.summary: Package SwiftPM macOS apps into signed, runnable bundles without an Xcode project.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from documented local macOS packaging scripts and Markdown command references. Confirmed risks involve sourcing version.env as shell code, writing signing credentials to predictable /tmp paths, and importing a signing identity into the login keychain. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Project version.env files are sourced as shell scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Parse only expected KEY=VALUE entries, reject shell syntax, and avoid source for untrusted project files.

remediation.issue: Signing keys and notarization keys are written to predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp -d with 700 permissions, set umask 077, store all secret files inside it, and clean quoted expanded paths.

remediation.issue: The development signing setup imports a certificate into the user login keychain.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit manual confirmation, prefer a dedicated temporary keychain, and document how to remove imported identities.

remediation.issue: Release scripts handle private signing and notarization credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Document that release scripts must be run locally after review, and never by automatic agent execution with live credentials.

content.value_statement: SwiftPM macOS apps need manual bundle, signing, and release steps outside Xcode. This skill supplies templates and guidance for scaffolding, packaging, notarizing, and appcast generation.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold a minimal SwiftPM macOS app layout with version metadata.
Build SwiftPM binaries for one or more macOS architectures.
Assemble a .app bundle with resources, frameworks, Info.plist, and entitlements.
Run a local package, launch, and process verification loop.
Generate .icns assets from an Icon Composer source file.
Prepare release signing, notarization, zip packaging, and Sparkle appcast steps.
limitations: Requires macOS and Apple developer tools for packaging, signing, and notarization.
Release workflows require valid developer credentials and Sparkle tooling.
Template scripts assume the documented project layout and may need project-specific edits.
Signing scripts should be reviewed before using real private keys or keychain access.

use_cases.title: Start a New SwiftPM App
use_cases.description: Create a clean app skeleton with package settings, source folders, resources, and version metadata.

use_cases.title: Package a Local Build
use_cases.description: Turn SwiftPM build output into a runnable .app bundle for testing without opening Xcode.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Pipeline
use_cases.description: Add signing, notarization, zip creation, and Sparkle appcast steps to a SwiftPM macOS release process.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a SwiftPM macOS app named MyApp. Include the folder layout, version file, and first packaging steps.

prompt_templates.title: Package for Local Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to package my SwiftPM macOS app for local testing. Explain which template scripts to copy and which variables to set.

prompt_templates.title: Add Release Signing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare signing and notarization for my SwiftPM macOS app. List required credentials, files, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to adapt the packaging templates for a menu bar app with resources, frameworks, universal builds, and Sparkle updates.

output_examples.input: Package a SwiftPM menu bar app for local testing.
output: A short packaging plan for the app layout.
The environment variables needed for menu bar behavior and bundle identity.
A verification checklist for launch and process checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare release signing for a SwiftPM macOS app.
output: A list of required Apple developer credentials.
The expected notarization and stapling sequence.
Safety notes for handling private keys and temporary files.

output_examples.input: Add Sparkle appcast support to my release flow.
output: A description of required Sparkle tools and private key settings.
The appcast generation sequence after a notarized zip exists.
Checks for version numbers, download URLs, and release notes.

best_practices: Review every copied script before running it with signing credentials.
Use ad hoc signing for local development and reserve Developer ID credentials for release builds.
Keep version numbers, bundle identifiers, and build numbers explicit in project configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not run release scripts with real credentials before inspecting temporary file handling.
Do not source configuration files from untrusted repositories without validation.
Do not publish appcasts or release zips before notarization and stapling checks pass.

faq.question: Does this skill require Xcode?
faq.answer: It avoids Xcode projects, but some templates require Xcode tools or command line tools.

faq.question: Can it create a new SwiftPM app?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a bootstrap layout and references for package, source, resource, and version files.

faq.question: Can it sign and notarize releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides release templates, but you must supply valid Apple developer credentials.

faq.question: Does it support universal binaries?
faq.answer: Yes. The packaging templates include architecture settings for arm64 and x86_64 builds.

faq.question: Does it generate Sparkle appcasts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an appcast template that expects Sparkle tools and a local private key file.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review scripts first because release paths can handle private keys and keychain changes.
